A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabICL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original TabICL classification results, runtime and memory measurements, and empirical analyses of learned representations.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results and adds tree-prior and curriculum ablations, ensemble-size experiments, and random-forest extensions.

M1.justification: Appendix G adds the TabICL-RF adaptation, combining tree partitioning, localized ICL predictions, and validation-based adaptive pruning. The main three-transformer architecture, synthetic-data generators, and hierarchical classification procedure remain unchanged; Appendix E.3 elaborates the existing hierarchy.

E1.justification: Both versions use TALENT classification datasets, the same synthetic-data families, and the same large-table memory scenarios. Development datasets excluded from v2's main aggregate remain evaluated in Appendix F, and the new analyses reuse existing coverage. Aggregate membership changes concern the evaluation protocol.

E2.justification: Figure 5 and Appendix I add TabM, LoCalPFN, and TuneTables to reported comparisons; LoCalPFN and TuneTables enter only accuracy rankings. Appendix G additionally evaluates TabPFNv2-RF, substantially strengthening the comparison with scalable alternatives on large datasets.

E3.justification: Reported stage-one pretraining increases from 100K to 160K steps and changes from warmup/cosine decay to cosine restarts. v2 introduces a 20K-step prior ablation, ensemble-size sweeps, and RF experiments with four-member foundation-model ensembles and adaptive pruning. It also excludes development datasets from the main aggregate. The stated counts remain inconsistent: removing 15 from 188 does not yield 171, and 116 small plus 53 large datasets totals 169.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained RoPE case study, metafeature analyses, and memory experiments, v2 adds tests of tree-based SCMs and curriculum stages in Section 5.3 and Figures 9–10/E.2. Appendices G and H add RF-extension analysis and ensemble-size sensitivity, substantially expanding examination of design choices.

E5.justification: Both versions report bootstrap medians with 10%/90% intervals for metafeature fits and Wilcoxon–Holm tests at significance level 0.05 for rank diagrams. The additional results do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice, seed disclosure, or repeated-run count.

E6.justification: Aggregate accuracy ranks for TabICL/TabPFNv2 change from 6.28/6.32 in v1 Figure E.1 to 6.95/7.17 in v2 Figure I.1. These use changed cohorts and comparators, so they are not same-setting performance changes. New results include curriculum-stage ranks of 11.40, 7.46, and 6.95, RF-extension outcomes, ensemble-size effects, and per-dataset scores in Table F.1.

T1.justification: New Section 3.5 derives componentwise complexity and distinguishes TabICL's O(nm^2 + n^2) cost from TabPFNv2's O(nm^2 + n^2m). Appendix B correspondingly revises v1 Appendix A's shared attention-cost motivation. This is a focused analytical addition rather than a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain scalable two-stage tabular ICL, distribution-aware embeddings, handling up to 500K samples and 500 features, and performance comparable to TabPFNv2 with faster inference. Updated benchmark counts and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for TabPFNv2's greater ensemble benefit, acknowledges curriculum-related degradation on some small datasets, and identifies possible disadvantages from mean imputation and withholding categorical metadata from TabPFNv2. The RoPE permutation-invariance limitation was already discussed in v1 and is additionally emphasized in v2's conclusion.

D1.justification: The abstract newly reports availability of pretraining code, extending the previously advertised inference code and pretrained weights. Appendices E.1, E.3, and G add explicit learning-rate parameters, hierarchical-node data and target handling, and RF settings. Reported pretraining time changes from two weeks to 20 days, substantially expanding information about reproducing training and extensions.

R1.justification: v2 adds Grinsztajn's 2024 thesis as explicit inspiration for tree-based SCMs; v1 acknowledged his contribution without citing that work. New Appendix A consolidates and extends comparison with TabPFNv2 across architecture, label fusion, pretraining, and scalability, while the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted prose edits, renames Section 2.3, expands explanations and limitations, and adds subsections within the existing narrative. Appendices are reorganized and renumbered, but most retained exposition and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 9–10, E.2, G.1, and H.1 and Table F.1, substantially expanding the visual evidence. It also expands baseline displays, redraws the stage-one learning-rate panel, and revises architecture labels and figure placement. The synthetic-data and memory plots are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct ablation support for its tree prior and curriculum; v2 adds these tests, ensemble sensitivity, and a stronger TabPFNv2-RF comparison. Separating development datasets, adding explicit complexity analysis, and reporting pretraining-code availability further strengthen evaluation and reproducibility. Unreconciled dataset counts weaken protocol clarity, but the substantial gains in validation and transparency outweigh this limitation.
